fixes.explanation: Yes, baker! "After Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions." (Job 42:10) Notice what comes first: Job prayed for his friends. Then the verse says the LORD restored his prosperity and doubled his former possessions. So the word that fits the blank is "restores."

True, baker! "So the LORD blessed Job’s latter days more than his first." (Job 42:12) Then the verse lists what Job owned: 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys. The latter days were blessed even more than the first. That makes this statement True.

Tenth would be a LOT of generations, friend, but the text says less. "After this, Job lived 140 years and saw his children and their children to the fourth generation." (Job 42:16) Job saw to the fourth generation. So the answer is the fourth generation, not the tenth.
